verdict.rationale: Bitwarden's own docs show vault export for backup and mention importing from 'encrypted exports', so encrypted backups exist as a first-party capability. A community comment calls it an 'e2ee password manager', but no documentation confirms the vendor never holds the key or describes the encryption design. Missing for 10: documented zero-knowledge/vendor-never-holds-key guarantee for backups, published encryption design documentation (key derivation, ciphers), and evidence that exports are end-to-end encrypted rather than merely password-protected.

support.subject: As a security engineer, backups are end-to-end encrypted with a key the vendor never holds, and the encryption design is documented

citations.quote: Import logins and data from different password managers, other Bitwarden vaults, or encrypted exports
Export your vault data, including logins and notes, to back up important information
I move to the next ethical e2ee password manager if BitWarden turns its back on open source
